title: GLP-1 and Body-Weight Golden Evidence Map
research_question: Do GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce body weight in adults with overweight or obesity?

scope.population: Adults with overweight or obesity, with population extensions explicitly separated when diabetes, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or PMOS changes applicability.
scope.intervention: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment, centered on semaglutide; liraglutide and the dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide appear only as explicit endpoint or active-comparator context.
scope.outcome: Body-weight or anthropometric change during continued treatment; non-weight outcomes are included only when they delimit what weight-loss evidence does not establish.
scope.exclusions: No pediatric, pregnancy, post-discontinuation maintenance, cost-effectiveness, or class-wide safety conclusion is represented by this bounded map. Different primary outcomes are not treated as direct support or contradiction.

evidence_nodes.inclusion_rationale: Placebo-controlled STEP 5 evidence for semaglutide 2.4 mg at 104 weeks in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes.
Large placebo-controlled SELECT analysis extending semaglutide weight and anthropometric outcomes to 208 weeks in adults with established cardiovascular disease without diabetes.
Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling randomized semaglutide trials while preserving dose, duration, and heterogeneity limitations.
Uncontrolled real-world semaglutide cohort extending observation to adults with obesity both with and without type 2 diabetes.
Propensity-matched oral-semaglutide cohort in adults with HFrEF, type 2 diabetes, and obesity, using no GLP-1 receptor agonist as comparator.
Short, uncontrolled PMOS cohort showing a distinct female reproductive population in which body weight is measured alongside ovulatory outcomes.

Large propensity-matched real-world comparison placing semaglutide weight-loss magnitude beside tirzepatide without reclassifying an active-comparator result as placebo-controlled support or contradiction.
Systematic review and meta-analysis comparing GLP-1RA-based and lifestyle intervention categories on waist circumference, an anthropometric outcome distinct from body weight.
Randomized secondary analysis showing that liraglutide's role in weight maintenance does not by itself establish improved physical fitness; exercise arms produced the fitness improvements.

population_groups.label: Adults without diabetes in randomized semaglutide evidence
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: STEP 5 and Gao address general overweight or obesity eligibility; SELECT additionally requires established cardiovascular disease. These populations do not establish effects in adults with diabetes.

population_groups.label: Adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes or heart failure
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: These are observational extensions with different indications, formulations, and comparators; they do not erase the eligibility limits of the randomized semaglutide trials.

population_groups.label: Women with PMOS and elevated BMI
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: The PMOS cohort is uncontrolled and its distinguishing question concerns ovulatory function. Its body-weight finding is contextual, not evidence that STEP 5 or SELECT tested PMOS outcomes.

population_groups.label: Broader adult synthesis or post-diet weight-maintenance populations
population_groups.interpretation_boundary: The waist-circumference synthesis pools heterogeneous adult interventions, while the liraglutide analysis begins after diet-induced weight loss and evaluates fitness rather than primary weight reduction.

comparator_groups.label: Placebo or randomized control
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: The most direct comparative evidence, but behavioral co-intervention, trial eligibility, dose, duration, and pooled heterogeneity remain material.

comparator_groups.label: Within-subject baseline without a concurrent control
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: Observed change cannot isolate treatment effects from concurrent care, selection, regression to the mean, or other time-varying factors.

comparator_groups.label: No GLP-1 receptor agonist active-care comparator
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: Propensity matching improves comparability but does not remove residual confounding or turn the cohort into a randomized placebo-controlled trial.

comparator_groups.label: Tirzepatide active comparator
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: A relative-effect comparison between two active therapies contextualizes magnitude; it does not refute semaglutide-versus-placebo evidence.

comparator_groups.label: Heterogeneous intervention categories
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: Subgroup categories do not provide one uniform drug-versus-placebo estimate, and between-category differences were not statistically significant.

comparator_groups.label: Exercise and placebo factorial arms
comparator_groups.interpretation_boundary: The finding qualifies fitness expectations during weight maintenance and must not be read as a null body-weight result.

contradiction_assessment.statement: No reviewed record in this bounded selection directly contradicts the semaglutide-versus-placebo body-weight direction under a sufficiently aligned population, intervention, comparator, and outcome. Tirzepatide's larger active-comparator estimate and liraglutide's null fitness result are contextual or endpoint-specific qualifiers, not same-question contradictions. Absence of an identified contradiction is not evidence that contradictory literature does not exist.

limitations: All nine selected Evidence Records remain draft and require independent secondary review before the map can become reviewed.
The direct randomized evidence is centered on semaglutide and adults without diabetes; it cannot support an undifferentiated class-wide conclusion for every GLP-1 receptor agonist or population.
Three population extensions and the active-comparator record are observational and remain vulnerable to residual confounding.
The map records evidence during continued treatment and does not establish durability after treatment discontinuation.
Adverse events, discontinuation, access, cost, and patient preference are not covered comprehensively enough for benefit-harm conclusions.
The graph contains reviewed support and context links, but those links do not compute consensus or truth.
known_gaps: Independent secondary review of every selected Evidence Record and this map's inclusion judgments.
Direct evidence for post-discontinuation weight maintenance or regain.
Broader agent-level coverage beyond semaglutide, with drug, dose, formulation, and duration kept separate.
Systematic adverse-event and discontinuation evidence linked to the same populations and treatment windows.
Pediatric, pregnancy, frailty, and geographically diverse population coverage where scientifically and ethically appropriate.
A reviewed same-PICO contradictory result, if one exists; none was identified in the bounded current selection.

review.method: Curated selection from structurally validated Evidence Records and reviewer-authored Relationship Records, with explicit PICO, comparator, endpoint, limitation, and contradiction-boundary checks.
review.notes: The artifact is a provisional map of traceable records, not a scientific conclusion. Validation checks structure and references only; it does not endorse the scientific judgments recorded here.
